item.title: Two children injured in Civic House explosion
item.description: Two children have been injured in an explosion at Civic House yesterday. The Ministry of Employment, which is based in the building, says the children have sustained injuries reportedly consistent with electrical flash burns.
item.content:encoded:
Two children have been injured in an explosion at Civic House yesterday.

The Ministry of Employment, which is based in the building, says the children have sustained injuries reportedly consistent with electrical flash burns.

They say the children are currently receiving medical treatment and remain under observation at CWM Hospital.

The Ministry says relevant authorities are currently conducting investigations into the circumstances surrounding the incident, including the cause.

They add their offices located at Civic House Levels 1, 4 and 5 are temporarily closed until further notice.

Police and the National Fire Authority are yet to respond to our questions.

item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji's first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti's journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti shares her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono.

Dr Sikiti also shares the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She speaks about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

item.title: Man allegedly stabbed several times with scissors in Caubati
item.description: A man in his 40s allegedly stabbed another man several times with a pair of scissors during an argument in Caubati New Subdivision, with police saying both men were heavily intoxicated at the time. Police say the incident occurred on Saturday and involved a 26-year-old man, who was allegedly stabbed several times during the confrontation.
item.content:encoded:
A man in his 40s allegedly stabbed another man several times with a pair of scissors during an argument in Caubati New Subdivision, with police saying both men were heavily intoxicated at the time.

Police say the incident occurred on Saturday and involved a 26-year-old man, who was allegedly stabbed several times during the confrontation.

They say the suspect also sustained injuries in the ensuing scuffle, and both men were taken to CWM Hospital for treatment.

The suspect was later discharged from hospital and remains in police custody as investigations continue.

The incident is one of two recent cases being highlighted by the Fiji Police Force as a reminder of the dangers associated with excessive alcohol consumption, particularly its potential to contribute to violence and other offences.

In a separate incident, a 40-year-old man was arrested in Lami on Monday night for allegedly drinking alcohol in a public place.

Police say he is further alleged to have assaulted a police officer, damaged police uniforms, and verbally abused and threatened officers at the scene.

The man has been charged with one count each of drinking in a public place, serious assault, damaging property, and criminal intimidation.

He is expected to appear at the Suva Magistrates Court today.

Police are again urging members of the public to consume alcohol responsibly and in moderation, warning that excessive drinking can impair judgment and contribute to violence , disorder, and other threats to public safety.

item.title: Public urged to verify online information as misinformation becomes harder to detect
item.description: The public is being urged to verify information before sharing it online as misinformation and disinformation have become increasingly difficult to detect, particularly with the growing use of artificial intelligence. While responding to questions on the fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan on whether stronger laws and regulations are needed to deal with people spreading misin
item.content:encoded:
The public is being urged to verify information before sharing it online as misinformation and disinformation have become increasingly difficult to detect, particularly with the growing use of artificial intelligence.

While responding to questions on the fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan on whether stronger laws and regulations are needed to deal with people spreading misinformation and unverified information, Online Safety Commissioner Filipe Batiwale says while laws and policies can help discourage the spread of misinformation, disinformation and malinformation, members of the public also have a responsibility to check what they see and read online.

He says people should stop and verify information, check whether it comes from a reliable source and seek information directly from relevant organisations when necessary.

Batiwale says the Online Safety Commission can also assist with education and awareness on verifying online information.

Insert: Always verify the sources KK 8th Sept

Meanwhile, Fiji Law Reform Commissioner David Solvalu says there are already provisions dealing with misinformation in specific areas, including electoral laws and business practices.

However, Solvalu says social media has significantly changed the scale of the problem, as individuals can now create and spread large amounts of misinformation to influence public views and opinions.

Insert: Awareness and education is the best thing KK 8th Sept

Solvalu says this is difficult to regulate not only in Fiji but around the world, therefore, public education and awareness remain among the strongest ways of addressing the problem.

item.title: Taxi driver calls for legal taxi solution to stop pari operations
item.description: Taxi driver Inoke Moto is calling for authorities to stop illegal pari operators from carrying passengers and instead find a legal solution to meet the demand for transport after normal taxi operating hours. Moto raised this during the Fiji Taxi Zone Association meeting in Nausori, stressing that illegal operators should not be encouraged to break the law simply because there is demand for transpo
item.content:encoded:
Taxi driver Inoke Moto is calling for authorities to stop illegal pari operators from carrying passengers and instead find a legal solution to meet the demand for transport after normal taxi operating hours.

Moto raised this during the Fiji Taxi Zone Association meeting in Nausori, stressing that illegal operators should not be encouraged to break the law simply because there is demand for transport late at night and in the early hours of the morning.

He says his company has been issued 20 base letters and he intends to approach the Nausori Town Council to explore whether taxis can legally operate during the hours when pari operators are most active.

He says allowing properly authorised taxis to operate during these hours could provide a solution while ensuring operators comply with the law.

The operator says there is no justification for protecting or encouraging illegal operations when legal options can be explored.

He adds that discussions about the taxi industry should focus on finding solutions for legitimate taxi operators rather than defending illegal pari operators.
